summary: Grant Parker specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an MA from the University of Cape Town (1989–1991) and a PhD from Princeton University (1993–1999). He taught at Duke University (1999–2006) and joined Stanford University in 2006.

Graves Champney Haughton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College in 1812 and circa 1813–1815. He taught at the East India Company College (1817–1827) and co-founded and served as secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Gray Tuttle works in Tibetology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He earned a BA from Princeton and an MA from Harvard, studying under Leonard van der Kuijp, William C. Kirby, and Philip A. Kuhn, becoming an associate professor at Columbia in 2005.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Samuel David Luzzatto. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902 and founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873.

Greg Bailey is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Melbourne under J. Durham and also studied under Madeleine Biardeau. He held posts at La Trobe University (attested 1994, 2003–2004) and the University of Tübingen (1998).

Gregor Ahn specializes in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit at the University of Bonn and the University of Copenhagen, later serving as professor of comparative religion at Heidelberg University (1996–2025).

Gregorio Franzò was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore from 1901 to 1904, later teaching "materie letterarie" at the Liceo Classico Carducci Ricasoli.

Gregory Adam Scott works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and held attested posts in 2026 at the University of Edinburgh and the University of Manchester, where he was Senior Lecturer in Chinese Culture and History.

Gregory Forgues specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, Birgit Kellner, and various traditional teachers including Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu.

Gregory Hillis works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia in 1993, where he held an attested post in 2002, and was attested as a Continuing Lecturer at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.
Gregory L. Possehl was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied under Walter A. Fairservis, Jr. He served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania, with his post attested in 2006.

Gregory Max Seton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara, and the University of Oxford (D.Phil 2015), where his doctoral supervisors included Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.
Gregory Nagy is a linguist who studied at Indiana University Bloomington (circa 1958–1962) and Harvard University (circa 1962–1966). He held a post at Harvard University in 2025.

Gregory P. A. Levine specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University before taking up a post in 2003 at the University of California, Berkeley as an associate professor.

Gregory Price Grieve works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied at San Francisco State University and the University of Chicago, later joining the University of North Carolina at Greensboro in 2002 as Professor and Department Head.

Gregory Schopen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, holding posts at Indiana, Texas at Austin, and UCLA (1999–2019).

Grigorij Fedorovich Ilyin was an Indologist and historian who studied at Moscow State University under Peter Peterson and Igor Mikhailovich Reisner. He held posts at the Diplomatic Academy (1947–1953), the USSR Academy of Sciences (1952), and the University of Chicago (1953).

Grigorij Lukich Nakhutsrishvili was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Tbilisi State University (circa 1944–1949), where he began teaching in 1952 and became chair in 1976.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indologist, historian, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies and under George de Roerich. He held longtime posts at the Russian Academy of Sciences and Moscow State University.

Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indologist and art historian/archaeologist. She completed her doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as a professor from 1978 to 1991.
